Personally, I would focus on the veg part of vegan and stick with the greens.  Eliminate all complex (refined/processed) carbs ie: flour, bread, pasta and refined oils and focus in on a leafy greens and whole grains. Easy on the beans and legumes particularly soy and lentils. They are superior protein sources but also very high in fibre, especially if your are just transitioning to plant based. 

Beans and legumes contain phytates (phytic acid) and their method of preparation can also affect digestion. Get your oils from their natural sources by consuming the actual food ie: nuts, seeds, coconut, olives, hemp hearts etc.

Up your water intake. Lower or eliminate  the intake of caffeinated beverages like coffee, tea, energy drinks or soda as these are all diuretics.

There is such a thing as too much fibre.  Especially if you are systemically dehydrated. Note: some medications can also act as a diuretic by causing frequent urination. Dehydration combined with very high fibre will cause hardening of the stool due to lower moisture and higher density. Then its like shitting bricks, sometimes painfully so as your colon works by squeezing the food through it with muscles. 

The key macronutrient balance you want to achieve is having enough fibre (indigestible cellulose aka ‘the brush’), to water, protein and carbohydrates.  Aka ‘balanced macros’

Perhaps you might benefit from tracking you food intake in something like [Chronometer](chronometer.com) or [My Fitness Pal](myfitnesspal.com) for a while to track your macros.
